usability.verdict:
Not ready for handoff. The direction is strong and most journeys get simpler. Setup is now a server-computed track on Home, every call goes through a Call gate with the cost as a range, Top up opens a sheet in place with UPI first, and going live now needs a Publish gate with a diff and "where it goes live". Each page follows the one-primary rule, and the pages I checked (Home, Leads, Billing, Assistant, Cockpit) show a clear hierarchy in both the specs and the renders. Two problems block handoff:

1. **Flow Designer on tablet and phone.** 05-responsive specifies a tablet editor and quick fixes on phones. The two Flow Designer specs, the direction, 06-accessibility and 07-motion all specify a read-only Review mode instead. The PNG renders show three different phone layouts.
2. **The interim fix for autosave-into-live (F-FLOW-001).** This is the fix that ships first, and it is defined three incompatible ways. The direction and Flow Designer part 1 still keep the path where edits reach the live flow.

On large flows, the tooling is well conceived: Find, the Outline, frames, Tidy, minimap and level of detail. Two things undercut it. At Fit, titles truncate to about 10 characters, so the "readable at Fit" claim is not met. And text is re-scaled on every pan and zoom frame, which puts the 60 fps target for 150 steps at risk.

Other gaps:
- Step numbers are defined as both positional and stable.
- The same keys (Alt+Arrow, and [ ]) are bound to different actions in different places.
- Templates are only validated in an empty CI setting, not in a real new workspace.
- The call review queue has no defined behaviour after "Mark reviewed".
- The interim device-draft publish can silently overwrite a teammate's publish.

Mobile is good where it matters most: Leads, Call reports, Cockpit live, Billing and Rep console. It stays unresolved for the Flow Designer until the first blocker is settled.

issues.problem:
The Flow Designer's tablet and phone behaviour is defined twice, and the two definitions contradict each other. 05-responsive §1 R5/R6 and §10.2–10.13 specify: tablet (768–1023) is a full editor (canvas, step sheet, Add step sheet, Navigate/Arrange switch, bottom tool bar); phone allows editing step text and changing answer targets. Every other doc says tablet is read-only Review mode and phone is read-only Outline: the direction §6.5 responsive table and §8 ('Minimum editing width: 1024 px'), 04-flow-designer/01 D11, §3.2, §3.4 and §17, 04-flow-designer/02 §7.1 ('read-only sheet below 1024'), §16.1 and §21.3–21.4, 06-accessibility part 8, and 07-motion parts 6–7. The page layouts also differ between the docs:
- Phone: part 1 has an Outline|Canvas switch with a sticky Test/Publish bar above the BottomBar. Part 2 §21.4 and its render have the sticky bar and no BottomBar. 05 §10.5 has Outline·Map·Issues·Test tabs, Publish in a top state row, and the BottomBar.
- Tablet: part 1 stacks TopBar + 48 px flow header + an Outline|read-only canvas split. 05 replaces the TopBar with a 52 px flow header, uses a full-width canvas and adds a bottom tool bar.
- Full-screen mode: 05 §10.3 keeps one at ≥1280; part 1 X7 has none.
- Clean draft: 05 §10.8 hides Publish; part 2 §4.3 shows it aria-disabled with a reason.
- Test on phone: 05 includes 'Call my phone…'; part 2 §13.6 excludes it.
The renders disagree too: 05-responsive-flow-768.png and -390.png against 02-config-validation-lifecycle-mobile.png and mock §10 of 01-canvas-and-nodes. 05 also says 'No Flow Designer page spec exists yet', which is stale. A developer cannot build tablet or phone from this set.
issues.fix:
Make one decision and propagate it to every doc. My recommendation is to adopt 05 R5/R6. With Draft/Publish in place, a tablet or phone edit can no longer reach callers, which was the only reason for the 1024 px editing floor. The Outline is already required to be a complete editor, and managers need to fix a typo on a tablet that blocks Publish.
1. Rewrite direction §6.5 (responsive table) and §8 ('Minimum editing width').
2. Rewrite 04-flow-designer/01 D11, §3.2 tablet and phone wireframes, §3.3 column '<1024', §3.4 tablet and phone rows, §17 and the §19 layout criteria.
3. Rewrite 04-flow-designer/02 §7.1, §13.6 Responsive, §16.1, §17 and §21.3–21.4.
4. Rewrite 06-accessibility part 2 (F-RWD-003 row) and part 8 §Responsive.
5. Rewrite 07-motion part 6 (tablet wireframe and 'no drag') and part 7 (the 768–1023 row).
6. Choose one phone layout. I suggest 05's tabs with Publish in the state row, keeping the BottomBar, which matches R4 (Flows is a phone tab).
7. Choose one clean-draft Publish state: aria-disabled with its reason, as in part 2 §4.3.
8. Choose one full-screen rule: none, as in part 1 X7.
9. Delete the 'No Flow Designer page spec exists' sentence and re-render every flow PNG from one mock.

issues.problem:
The interim behaviour before revisions ship is the first thing to ship for the critical F-FLOW-001, and three docs define it three incompatible ways:
- Direction §8 'Interim behaviour' says 'Publish is today's ACTIVATE behind the Publish gate' and 'the Draft chip stays hidden'. Autosave therefore still writes the flow that live calls read.
- Part 1 §3.3 ('Before the revisions backend ships… runs today's ACTIVATE') agrees. Part 1 §4.4 even gives the live note the interim copy 'Active flow. Changes apply to calls immediately.'
- Part 2 §4.9 (Interim I1) and R1 hold edits in IndexedDB until Publish, which then writes the flow with a PUT. It turns ACTIVATE into 'Make my Cockpit default', and the live note reads 'Edits stay on this device until you publish.'
The shell Home §13.3 counts step 1 as done by 'an activated flow', which follows the first reading. Whoever builds from the direction or part 1 ships a designer where edits still reach callers mid-edit.
issues.fix:
Make I1 the only interim everywhere.
1. Direction §8: replace the two interim bullets with the I1 summary, and change the 'Save in Flow Builder' decision to 'Autosave goes to the Draft (on this device until revisions ship)'.
2. Part 1 §3.3 Publish states: 'Before revisions ship the label is Publish… and it writes the device draft to the flow through the gate (P2 §4.9)'.
3. Part 1 §4.4: interim live note 'Edits stay on this device until you publish. Callers hear the saved flow.' in --text-2, not warning.
4. 03-pages/00-app-shell-ia §13.3 step 1 done-when (interim): 'a publish recorded through the Publish gate'.
5. Add one acceptance criterion in part 1 §19: with revisions off, 20 edits send zero network writes until the gate's Publish.

issues.problem:
Interim I1 (§4.9) has no conflict protection, and FD2 (If-Match) is missing, so Publish is a last-write-wins PUT. Two failure cases follow:
- Author A keeps a device draft for a day while author B edits in another browser and publishes. When A publishes, the gate's diff is computed against 'the last published server copy', so B's work shows up as rows A may not notice. A's PUT then silently reverts B's live changes.
- The device draft is invisible from any other browser. A teammate told 'I fixed the flow' sees nothing. If IndexedDB is unavailable (private window, blocked storage), 'Saved on this device' is false.
issues.fix:
In §4.9:
1. When a device draft starts, record the server copy's updated_at and content hash as its base.
2. Opening the Publish gate re-fetches the server copy. If it differs from the base, add a blocking check row: 'This flow was published from another browser at 11:31 am. Your draft is based on an older copy. Review changes', with the choices 'Re-apply my changes on top' (a 3-way merge per step, conflicts listed) or 'Discard my draft'.
3. On /flows, show an 'Unpublished edits on this device' tag per flow.
4. If IndexedDB throws, the chip reads 'Not saved · this tab only' in danger tone, beforeunload is registered, and Publish stays available.
5. Add an acceptance criterion covering the two-browser overwrite case.

issues.problem: Step-number semantics contradict each other. Part 1 D7 makes `#n` positional: it follows call order and 'can change when steps are added'. Part 2 §7.1, §12.2 and §16.2 call it 'the stable step number… which never change[s]', and R12 claims part 1 agrees. The numbers are used across the product: in validator and 422 messages ('#5 Ask about budget'), Find ('9' jumps to step 9), Outline reference rows, the Publish diff, version history, Call reports' 'Field · step n' columns and Analytics per-step drop-off. If they renumber on every insertion, 'fix step 9' said in chat, a saved Problems message or a Call report column header points at a different step after the next edit or version.
issues.fix: Make the visible `#n` a stable per-flow sequence id. It is assigned at creation as max+1, never reused, unchanged by Tidy, edits or publishing, and carried across versions, so Call reports and History stay valid. Express call order separately: in Outline order, arrow-key roving order, and the aria-label 'Step 3 of 14 in call order'. Rewrite part 1 D7, §5.1 (phase line) and §11.1, and part 2 R12, to say this. Add the rule that Find matches both '#9' and titles.

issues.problem:
Several keyboard shortcuts are bound twice in the designer:
- Alt+↓/Alt+↑ means 'Next/previous issue' (§11.2, part 2 §12.4, §18 and R7).
- The same keys mean 'Alt+Arrow moves the selection by 16 px' (§10.4 and §11.2, in the same table).
- They also mean 'move a step within a chain' in the Outline (part 2 §16.3) and 'move the item' in the answer editor (part 2 §7.7).
- Compare mode uses `[`/`]` for previous/next change (part 2 §4.5), but `[` is the shell's global rail and sidebar toggle (00-app-shell-ia §3.8), and it stays active in focus mode.
Keyboard-only authors, the population that F-A11Y-001 is fixing, will get unpredictable results.
issues.fix: Keep Alt+Arrow for 'move' everywhere: nudging on the canvas, and reordering in the Outline and the answer editor. That is one consistent meaning. Move issue navigation to a non-conflicting pair scoped to the designer, such as Alt+. / Alt+, (listed in the `?` sheet and in the Problems bar tooltips). Suppress the shell `[` shortcut while the Flow Designer is in focus mode; the rail overlay stays available from its button. Rewrite the §11.2 table, part 2 §12.4, §18 and R7, and add a lint test that fails on duplicate bindings within one context.

issues.problem: Large flows are not readable at Fit. The Block band (§5.5) keeps titles at 12 px, but inside a node box that shrinks with zoom. In the spec's own render (01-canvas-and-nodes-full.png, 'Large flows', 23 steps at 38%), titles truncate to about 10 characters: 'Ask prefer…', 'Ask about …', 'Greet the c…', 'Good time …', 'Ready to vi…'. `#n` is dropped in that band. Steps with shared prefixes, which are common ('Ask about budget' and 'Ask about area'), become indistinguishable. The §19 criterion 'Fit shows every step with a readable 12 px title' is met on paper but not in use, and Flow B has 35 steps.
issues.fix:
In the Block band:
1. Render the title as a counter-scaled overlay at least 140 screen px wide, wrapping to two lines, prefixed with `#n`. It may extend into the rank gap; where two labels would collide, the lower-priority one hides and reappears on hover or focus.
2. Size --layout-rank-gap so that at 0.35 zoom a 140 px label fits between layers.
3. Change §19 to: 'At Fit on Flow B, every visible label shows ≥20 characters or the full title, and no two visible labels are identical'.
4. Open flows with more than 20 steps at ≥1280 with the Outline panel docked (a remembered preference).

issues.problem: Continuous counter-scaling puts large-flow speed at risk. §5.5 writes --zoom to the viewport element on every onMove, and every text role uses `font-size: max(size, calc(12px / var(--zoom)))`. The focus outline also uses calc(2px / zoom). Below about 0.92 zoom, every pan or pinch frame therefore invalidates style and re-lays out text for every visible step. When zoomed out, the whole flow is visible, so onlyRenderVisibleElements does not help. That conflicts with §12.7's target of 60 fps with 150 steps on an integrated-graphics 1366×768 laptop, and 'boxes never change size' does not remove the text re-layout.
issues.fix: During a gesture, let text scale with the viewport transform. Write --zoom, quantised to 0.05, only on onMoveEnd and when the band changes, or rAF-throttle it to at most one write per 100 ms. Alternatively, use fixed flow-unit sizes per band (the band's minimum zoom sets the size) so zooming never changes font-size. Add a §19 criterion measured with the level-of-detail clamp active: pinch-zoom from 1.0 to 0.25 on 150 steps with 4× CPU throttle keeps ≥50 fps and has no long task over 50 ms.

issues.problem:
Templates are validated only in isolation, so the first-run 'Publish a flow' journey can start with errors. Part 1 §13.3 and part 2 §12.2 promise that every template has zero errors and zero warnings, but CI runs them outside any workspace. In a real new workspace, workspace-dependent rules fire as soon as a template is created:
- An Inbound call trigger with no number (W08).
- Support FAQ's Knowledge lookup with no indexed source (E13, an error).
- Site visit's WhatsApp confirmation with no approved template (E12/W01).
- Book meeting with no calendar connected (W02).
Home §13.3 pre-selects a template from the workspace goal, so the first-run user's first Publish can be blocked or need warning ticks. §15.3 'Create flow' says nothing about adapting templates to the workspace.
issues.fix:
In §15.3:
1. Template instantiation adapts to the workspace. Bind the workspace's only verified unbound number, or fall back to Outbound batch. Book meeting defaults to 'Set hours'. WhatsApp confirmation is off unless connected. Knowledge lookup uses 'This step's Q&A' with sample Q&A.
2. Each TemplateCard shows a 'Needs: Google Calendar · approved WhatsApp template' line computed from the workspace.
3. The goal pre-selection prefers templates whose needs are met.
4. Acceptance: in an empty workspace, creating every template yields 0 errors, and at most W08 when no number exists.

issues.problem:
The blank-flow first view, the first screen of 'build a flow', is defined three ways:
- Part 1 §13.2: Trigger connected to an Outcome, a '+' on the connection, and an empty-state card with Add Speak / Add Question. No errors.
- Part 2 §17 'First use': Trigger and Outcome unconnected, the inspector on the trigger, and the issues chip red with '1 error (E03)'.
- 05-responsive §10.8: 'only a Trigger' plus a hint, and on phones 'Add steps on a tablet or computer'.
A new author meeting a red error chip before doing anything is exactly the false-state noise the direction forbids.
issues.fix: Adopt part 1 §13.2 everywhere. Rewrite part 2 §17 'Designer · First use' and 05-responsive §10.8 'Empty flow' to match: connected Trigger→Outcome, the card, and an issues chip at 'No issues', or the Q2 warning 'Choose what this call records' if that rule ships. The phone copy follows whichever responsive decision the first blocker settles.

issues.problem:
The 'review calls' journey stops at one call. The QA job (§2.1) is to work through the Needs review view, but the sheet footer (§2.6.4) offers only 'Mark reviewed' (secondary) and never advances. Several behaviours are undefined:
- What happens to the reviewed row in the Needs review view: does it vanish under the cursor and shift the list?
- Do the view count and ViewSummary update?
- How do the sheet's ⌃⌄ previous/next behave when the current call leaves the result set?
Reviewing 9 calls takes about 3 actions per call, and the list may jump.
issues.fix:
In §2.6.4 and §2.7:
1. In the Needs review view, the footer action becomes 'Mark reviewed and next' (secondary, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter). It opens the next unreviewed call and moves focus to its title.
2. The reviewed row stays in the table with a 'Reviewed · Undo' tag until the view is refreshed or re-entered, with no reflow; the tab count and ViewSummary decrement at once.
3. ⌃⌄ navigate over the snapshot taken when the sheet opened.
4. After the last call: 'All 9 calls reviewed' with 'Back to Call reports'.
5. Add these to §2.13 acceptance.

issues.problem: Below 1280, the Flow Designer loses the signals that prove draft and live are separate. §10.5 and §10.7 fold the live note into the Live chip's popover and make SaveState icon-only at 1024–1279 and on tablet. The render 05-responsive-flow-1024.png shows 'Draft · 3 changes ▾ [check icon] ● Live v7', with nothing saying which one you are editing or that callers are unaffected. Part 1 §4.4 instead keeps 'Callers hear v7 until you publish. Compare' at 1024–1279, and part 1 §3.3 keeps the word 'Saved'.
issues.fix: At every width ≥768, keep a one-line live note ('Callers hear v7 until you publish'), placed in the phase-ruler row as part 1 does. SaveState always keeps a word ('Saved'; the time may move to the tooltip). The inspector or step-sheet footer 'Edits save to the draft' appears in every mode. Update §10.5, §10.7 (FlowHeader Compact/Tablet rows) and the 1024 render.

issues.problem: The flow header at ≥1280 carries a wallet chip (₹2,340.50) as its 12th item (§3.3 row 8, visible in 01-canvas-and-nodes-desktop.png) and between the Live chip and the Issues/Test/Publish cluster. It is unrelated to editing, adds noise to the one place that must read 'what's live / what I changed / can I publish', and is already hidden at 1024–1279 unless low.
issues.fix: Use the 1024–1279 rule at every width. Show the wallet chip in the designer only when the wallet is low, empty or blocked, or while the Test panel is in 'Call my phone' mode. Update the §3.3 table and the 1440/1280 wireframes.

issues.problem: The docs disagree on editing during a test run. Part 1 §14 says 'Test running… editing stays allowed'. Part 2 §14.2 says the Delete key 'does nothing while a test is running… Stop the test to edit'. Part 2 §13.4 says marks stay until the author edits, which implies editing is allowed.
issues.fix: Choose 'editing allowed' (it matches the author's fix-and-retest loop). Any edit during a run shows 'Draft changed during this test · Restart' in the Test panel, and the run is recorded as 'before your last change'. Remove the Delete-key exception in §14.2.

issues.problem: Top-up targets disagree. Cockpit §1.3's readiness row ('Top up → /billing?topup=1') and the Leads findings row route Top up to /billing?topup=1, which navigates away from a half-configured New call card. Shell D9, §6.4 and Billing §2.4 require the Top-up sheet to open in place and return focus to the now-enabled call control.
issues.fix: Replace every page-spec target '/billing?topup=1' with 'openTopUp({ source }) (in place, shell §6.4)', in Cockpit §1.3, §2.2 and §4 and in Leads part 1 and part 4. Keep /billing/wallet?topup=1 only for links from outside the app. Add a Cockpit acceptance criterion: after topping up from the Wallet row, the card's picks are unchanged and focus is on the primary.

issues.problem: In the Cockpit, the builder's first test call is hidden in a combobox. With Contact empty, the primary shows 'Place call…', disabled with 'Choose a lead or enter a number.' (§3.3). 'My phone' is found only by opening the Contact combobox's 'You' group, although §2.1 lists 'hear it before a customer does' as a primary job.
issues.fix: When Contact is empty and a verified own number exists, show a one-tap text button 'Call my phone…' under the Contact field. It fills the target, and the gate still applies. Arriving from Flows 'Test… › Call my phone' or from Home step 4 pre-fills the target through ?new=1&target=me.

issues.problem: On Home, time to first value is gated by paperwork. 'Call yourself' (§13.3 step 4) is blocked until number verification (Owned → Compliance → Authorized, which may take days) and a top-up. The only immediate way to hear the agent is a small 'Talk in browser instead' link that 'doesn't complete this step'. A new workspace can sit for days without hearing its own agent from the track.
issues.fix: While step 4 is blocked, show 'Hear it in your browser' as a visible secondary button, not a link, on step 4 and on step 1's done line. It opens a Browser test of the published flow. Add expected-time copy on step 2 ('Review usually takes 1–2 working days', only if true). Do not count the browser test toward the five checks.

issues.problem: The 'Live' wording rule contradicts the render. §5.5 says 'nothing says Live until all five checks pass', but the Baseline segment 1 ('Live v1 · Site-visit qualifier') and Home step 1's done line ('v1 is live') say Live during setup. 00-app-shell-ia-desktop.png shows 'Live v1' next to 'Wallet ₹0 · calls paused'.
issues.fix: Restate the rule as: 'The workspace is never called live until all five checks pass; flow version tags (Live v1) are allowed because they are version states.' Or show 'Published v1' in both places until setup completes. Pick one and update §5.2, §5.5, §13.3 and the render.

issues.problem: The page's core verb is invisible at rest. The Leads job is to call the right leads (§1), but the header's only filled button is New lead, and the row 'Call…' action appears only on hover or focus (§4, §5.1). A first-time operator on a fine pointer sees no call affordance until they hover a row or select one.
issues.fix: In the pinned actions column, show 'Call…' permanently as a tertiary text button (--text-2) at Standard density. Keep hover-reveal only for ⋯. At minimum, show it on the Callbacks due and Not reached views. It still opens the Call gate.

issues.problem:
Some responsive numbers and zoom mappings disagree across docs:
- Phone rows per screen: direction §6.3 says ≥5, shell §3.5 says '5–6', 05 §3.4 says ≥8 (10 at 390×844), and Leads says ≥8 at 360×780.
- 200% zoom of 1440×900 (720 CSS px) is 'the tablet layout' in Cockpit §2.4 but the phone shell in 05 §2.6 and shell §3.4.
- 200% zoom of 1280 is 'Review mode' in part 2 §20, but it resolves to 640 CSS px, which is phone mode.
- The Cockpit route is still /dashboard in 01-agent-cockpit §1.4 and §8 Q1, although shell D2 decides a 308 redirect to /cockpit.
issues.fix:
Make 05 canonical for rows and zoom mapping, and correct the other docs:
- Cockpit §2.4, last paragraph: 720 CSS px gets the phone layout.
- Shell §3.5 phone row: ≥8 rows once the header scrolls away.
- Direction §6.3: ≥8.
- Part 2 §20: 200% of 1280 gets phone mode.
- Cockpit §1.4 and §8: /cockpit is canonical, and /dashboard 308-redirects to it.

system.verdict: Not ready for handoff. The token pipeline is solid: I rebuilt tokens.json into a scratch copy, and tokens.css, tailwind.theme.css and tailwind.preset.js came out byte-identical to the committed files, and all 396 contrast pairs pass in both themes. The a11y model (focus separate from selection, the single-key registry, focus management, target-size rules) is well above average. The problems are at the system level: the specs contradict each other on the things a developer must get right first. (1) base.css still re-bases rem to 14 px. Three specs flag this, none fixed it, and two mocks and their PNGs render every size at 87.5%. (2) The Gate, the direction's central safety component, has no spec. Five page specs each define their own version. (3) The Flow Designer's tablet and phone capability, the canvas ARIA role, the canvas key map and the pre-revisions interim behaviour (the fix for critical F-FLOW-001) are each defined differently in 01, 02, 05 and 06. (4) About 60 tokens the specs rely on don't exist in tokens.json, and some conflict with each other. Fix the blockers, then run one pass to update the direction and foundations from the reconciliation tables, which were written but never applied to the documents they amend.

issues.problem: `html { font: var(--type-body-14) }` sets the root to 14 px (0.875rem is resolved against the initial 16 px), so every rem token renders at 87.5%. meta-12 comes out at 10.5 px (below the 12 px floor), label-13 at 11.4 px and title-20 at 17.5 px. It also breaks the user's browser text size (F-VIS-002, WCAG 1.4.4). Three specs flag it (02-components-core §1.10, 02-components-data-nav §0.6, 06-accessibility §18 and R8), but base.css was never fixed. Every mock works around it with an inline `html{font-size:100%}` except components/overlay.html and tokens/foundations.html, which load base.css without the patch. So the foundations specimen ('every token rendered') and the overlay PNGs show every size about 12% too small.
issues.fix: In base.css move the `font:` and `letter-spacing` declarations from `html` to `body`, and add `html { font-size: 100%; }`. Remove the per-mock overrides. Re-render foundations-{light,dark,mobile}.png and overlay-{light,dark,mobile}.png. Add the CT-03 assertion (html computes to 16 px, meta-12 to 12 px) to CI. Close the open question in core §11 (item 8) and data-nav §0.6.

issues.problem: The Gate spec is missing. Direction P3 says Call gate, Publish gate and Setup track are 'one component', and it sits in the §8 build order. Core §0, overlay §1.1 and §3.1, and data-nav §0.1 all defer to 'the Gate spec', which doesn't exist. Instead each page defines its own: CallGate/GateChecklist/GateCheckRow in 03-pages/01-agent-cockpit §7.2, a separate Call gate anatomy in 03-pages/03-leads §6.10, PublishGate in 04-flow-designer/02 §24, SetupTrack in 03-pages/00-app-shell-ia, AddAgentGate in 03-pages/07, the Top-up sheet 'as the money gate' in 03-pages/05 R6, and ApprovalCard in 03-pages/02 ('the Gate spec is not written yet'). They diverge. Check kinds are pass/blocking/advisory/checking/unknown in Cockpit but must-pass/adjusted/advisory in Leads. Elevation is e2 in Leads and overlay §1 but e3 in foundations §8 and the direction. Leads says global blockers never open the gate (§6.10) yet lists 'Wallet is ₹0' as an in-gate Blocked state (§7.4).
issues.fix: Write spec/02-components-gate.md. It owns GateChecklist and GateCheckRow, with one check-kind enum: pass | blocking | advisory | adjusted | checking | unknown. It also owns the CallGate (single and batch), PublishGate, SetupTrack, AddAgentGate and money-gate variants; containers per breakpoint (popover 400 / sheet 640 / bottom sheet); one elevation (e3) and radius (12); the cost-line grammar; ⌘/Ctrl+Enter; initial focus on the heading; the idempotency key; the gate-token expiry; and one wallet-₹0 rule (for example 'the entry point is aria-disabled; if the wallet drops while the gate is open, show the blocked row'). Then replace the page-level definitions with references and 'configuration' tables only.

issues.problem: The Flow Designer's tablet and phone capability is defined three different ways. 00-design-direction §6.5 and §8, 04-flow-designer/01 D11, §3.2 and §8.4, 04-flow-designer/02 §21.3, and 06-accessibility §18 and §19.B all say: 768–1023 is read-only Review mode, editing needs ≥1024, and phones get Outline, text test and Publish. 05-responsive R5 and R6, §10.2 and §10.6 say tablets get full editing (Arrange mode, Add step sheet, editable step sheet) and phones can edit text and re-point answers. 04-flow-designer/02 L12 calls the Outline, which is the phone view, a full editor that can add, reorder and delete steps. 02 §13 says 'Call my phone' stays in the Cockpit on phones, while 05 §10.6 offers it on phones through a bottom-sheet gate. 05 §20 records 'reconciliations' against D and O, but not against 01, 02 or 06, and none of the owning documents were updated.
issues.fix: Get the owner's decision (05 open questions 1 and 2). Then make one capability matrix the only source, in 04-flow-designer/02 §21 or in 05 §10.6, and update direction §6.5 and §8 ('minimum editing width'), 01 D11, §3.2, §8.4 ('below 1024 it never opens') and §20.1 (FlowCanvas `mode`), 02 L12 and §13 responsive, and 06 §18 and §19.B. If tablets edit, 06 needs keyboard and AT rules for Arrange mode and the editable step sheet. Remove the Specimen's 'Editing needs 1024' frame.

issues.problem: The ARIA model for the canvas, the fix for critical F-A11Y-001, contradicts itself across three documents. 01 §3.1 and §16.1 always put `role="application"` with aria-roledescription 'flow canvas' on the canvas. 06-accessibility §6.1 says 'No role="application" anywhere': the canvas is a `<section aria-labelledby>` with a hidden h2 'Canvas' (§9.6). 05-responsive §10.11 says 'role="application" only while focus is inside it'. A developer can't satisfy all three, and screen-reader behaviour (browse mode versus focus mode) depends entirely on this choice.
issues.fix: Adopt 06's model, which works with standard roles: steps are role=group with aria-roledescription=step inside a roving tab stop, sockets are buttons and the Outline is a tree. Delete role=application from 01 §3.1 (region table), §16.1 and §20.1, and from 05 §10.11. Keep one aria-describedby instruction string, defined once in 06 §9.6, and have 01 reference it.

issues.problem: There are three different interim behaviours for the period before the revisions backend ships, which is the period that matters for critical F-FLOW-001. (a) Direction §8 and overlay §18.2: the Draft chip stays hidden and Publish is ACTIVATE behind the gate. (b) 01 §4.4: the live note reads 'Active flow. Changes apply to calls immediately.', so edits still go live, and 03-pages/00-app-shell-ia §5.2 shows the Baseline as 'Active flow'. (c) 02 §4.9 (I1): edits stay on this device until Publish, with a 'Draft on this device · 3 changes' chip and 'Saved on this device 11:24 am'. That label isn't in overlay §18.4's `SaveStatus` union ('saved' | 'dirty' | 'saving' | 'error' | 'new' | 'offline' | 'conflict'). Offline copy also differs: 'Offline · 3 edits on this device' in O §18.1 versus 'Offline · 2 edits waiting' in 05 §10.8.
issues.fix: Adopt I1 everywhere (it is the only option that removes F-FLOW-001 before the backend ships). Update direction §8 'Interim behaviour'. In overlay §18.1, §18.2 and §18.4, add a `device` save status and a `device` VersionChip variant with their copy. Change 01 §4.4's interim live note to 02's copy ('Edits stay on this device until you publish. Callers hear the saved flow.'), and change the shell's Baseline interim segment to 'Saved flow · Site-visit qualifier'. Pick one offline string.

issues.problem: tokens.json is still v1.0.0, but the specs use about 60 tokens that don't exist in tokens.json or tokens.css. Examples: --dur-spin, --timing-skeleton-min, --live-pulse-cycles and --shift-sheet (07 calls these 'accepted'); --size-node-trigger/logic/action/outcome, --size-answer-row, --edge-width/-dash/-hover/-radius, --zoom-min/-max, --lod-full/-compact and --grid-snap (01 §20.2); --size-test-panel and --size-compare-bar (02); --nav-hover-bg/--nav-active-bg/--nav-active-border, which are theme-split and used by 03-pages/06-settings; --qr-fg/--qr-bg; --type-display-48, --size-auth-panel and --section-pad-y (08); --size-softphone, --timing-state-announce and --timing-call-stale (01-cockpit); --danger-hover (core); --size-chart-*, --size-turn-gutter and --size-view-summary; --size-scrollrow-fade and --size-sheet-step (05); and the `interaction` JS group. Some requests conflict: --timing-debounce versus the existing --timing-validate-debounce, and three names for the flow left panel. Several (the nav aliases, --danger-hover, --qr-*) change colour pairs that check-contrast.mjs has never checked. The rule 'every value is a token' and the lint rule 'no arbitrary values' can't both hold until these exist.
issues.fix: Cut tokens.json v1.1.0. Add every accepted request under `component.*`, `interaction` and `timing`, giving each exactly one name (drop --timing-debounce and keep --timing-validate-debounce; see the left-panel issue). Emit them with build-tokens.mjs and add the new colour pairs to check-contrast.mjs. Replace the 'Token requests' sections in 02-*, 03-pages/*, 04-*, 05 and 07 with a single register table in 01-foundations (§18: token, value, owner spec, status).

issues.problem: Opacity is applied to text on the canvas. Unreachable steps render their body at --opacity-unreachable 0.5 (§5.4), and phase emphasis or Find dims other steps to --opacity-dim 0.4 (§4.4, §7.2; foundations §10 allows this for 'whole regions'). Composited over the canvas, that gives (light) title 3.48:1, text-2 2.50:1 and text-3 2.12:1 at 0.5, and 2.59, 2.03 and 1.79 at 0.4. Dark gives 4.55, 3.19 and 2.38 at 0.5, and 3.35, 2.48 and 1.95 at 0.4. That fails WCAG 1.4.3. Unreachable steps are active errors the user must fix, not inactive components. It also breaks foundations §1.3 rule 2 ('No alpha on text, ever'), and 06 §13.1 rule 6 (CT-02: zero text nodes below 4.5:1 on rendered pages) would fail on any flow with an unreachable step.
issues.fix: Never put opacity on a container that holds text. Unreachable: full opacity, --surface-2 fill, title in --text, phase line in --text-3 (≥4.70:1), hollow input port, plus the existing danger badge. Apply --opacity-unreachable only to the glyph tile, sockets and incoming or outgoing connectors. Dimmed: dim only connectors, glyph tiles and sockets, and give non-emphasised steps the --surface-2 fill. Rewrite foundations §10 to 'graphics only, never an ancestor of text'. Add an unreachable plus dimmed fixture to CT-02.

issues.problem: The canvas key map contradicts itself and 06. In 01 §11.2, Alt+↓/↑ means next/previous issue, and in the same table Alt+Arrow moves the selection by 16 px. 01 defines Space as 'select only the focused step' (Shift+Space toggles), while 06 §9.6 has Space toggle selection. 06 §9.6 and R12 move steps with `M` Move mode, which 01 doesn't list. The single-character shortcuts 01 lists (§11.1: +, −; §11.2: Shift+1/2/0) and `M` for the canvas are missing from 06 §8.2's registry, so the 2.1.4 switch wouldn't reach them. 07 §0 records the conflict and leaves it open (Q5).
issues.fix: Make 06 §9.6 the only canvas key map and delete the duplicate tables in 01 §11.2 and 02 §16.5 and §18, leaving references. Resolve it as: Alt+↑/↓ = issues; `M` then arrows = move (drop Alt+Arrow); Space = toggle and Shift+Space = add to selection, or the reverse, but stated once. Add `+`, `−`, `Shift+1/2/0`, `M` (canvas) and `Alt+Delete` to the §8.2 registry so the switch and the generated `?` sheet cover them.

issues.problem: The rules for looping motion differ between the foundation docs and the later specs. Direction §5 and §6.2, foundations §11 ('--dur-pulse … the only loop'; 'perpetual motion only for the live dot'), data-nav §0.4 item 6 and §5.4 say the live dot pulses for as long as a call is live and nothing else loops. 06 §14.2 and 07 MD3 bound the pulse to 3 cycles (the --live-pulse-cycles token doesn't exist). Spinners and the indeterminate bar also loop (overlay §12 and §14, 07 M5). Spinner speed is given as one turn per --dur-pulse (1,600 ms) in core §1.7, but 800 ms (--dur-spin) in overlay §21, 06 §14.1 and 07 MD6.
issues.fix: Amend direction §5 ('Motion') and §7 anti-pattern 4, foundations §11, and data-nav §0.4 and §5.4 to 07's rules: a bounded 3-cycle pulse on the focal CallHeader only, and spinner or indeterminate-bar loops only while a user-started request is in flight. Set core §1.7 to --dur-spin 800 ms. Add --dur-spin and --live-pulse-cycles to tokens.json (see the token-register issue).

issues.problem: In forced colours, focus and selection become the same thing. base.css gives `[aria-selected=true]`, `[aria-current]` and `[data-selected]` a 2 px Highlight outline at −2 px, and focus is also a Highlight outline. In Windows contrast themes a focused row, a selected row and the current nav item look identical, and the current page's nav item looks permanently focused. That contradicts foundations §13 (selection is 'never an outline, so it never looks like focus') and direction P5/F-A11Y-007. Also, `[data-mark]{background-color:CanvasText}` fills free (hollow) and connected sockets alike, so the free-versus-connected state disappears.
issues.fix: In the forced-colors block, set selection and current to `background-color: SelectedItem; color: SelectedItemText; outline: none` (or a 4 px inline-start border in Highlight for rows and nav), and keep focus as a 2 px outline with offset. Add a `[data-mark="hollow"]` variant (`background: Canvas; border: 2px solid CanvasText`) for free sockets and ports. Update foundations §13 and 06 §13.3 to match, and add a VR-02 snapshot of focused plus selected in forced colours.

issues.problem: The legacy alias file overwrites live tokens. tokens.css defines the validated CVD-safe sentiment palette (--sentiment-positive green-500, --sentiment-neutral graphite-400/500, --sentiment-negative red-700/red-650). legacy-aliases.css is loaded after it (foundations §15.1 import order) with the same selector specificity (`:root, [data-theme]`) and redefines them as --success-text, --text-3 and --danger-text. For the whole migration release, charts therefore use unvalidated colours (dark negative becomes red-300, not red-650). The file's own lint rule ('any new use of a name in this file is an error') would also ban the canonical --sentiment-* names that data-nav charts use.
issues.fix: Delete the three --sentiment-* lines from legacy-aliases.css. The names already exist in tokens.css with the new values, just as --text-muted is handled. Exclude them from the legacy-name lint list, and change the foundations §15.6 table row to 'same names, new values'.

issues.problem: The in-app motion preference has two different specs and no CSS. 06 §14.3 specifies `data-motion="reduced"` with the menu 'Motion: System · Reduced'. 07 MD4 specifies `data-motion="reduce"` with 'Match system · Reduce motion'. Neither tokens.css nor base.css has a `[data-motion]` rule; they only zero --shift-*, --dur-trace and --dur-pulse and cap keyframes inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)`. So the setting would do nothing.
issues.fix: Pick `data-motion="reduce"` and one menu label. In build-tokens.mjs, emit the reduced-motion token block for both `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and `:root[data-motion="reduce"]`. Duplicate base.css's animation cap under `[data-motion="reduce"] *`. Have THEME_BOOT (foundations §15.3) set the attribute before paint. Update 06 §14.3 and 07 MD4 to the same wording.

issues.problem: The flow left panel (Outline, Add step, Variables, History) has three token names, three widths, and no definition. 01 §3.1 uses `--size-outline-panel` 280 'requested in P2 §24'. 02 §6, §8 and §16 use `--size-left-panel` 280 and point to 'part 1 §20.2', and 02 §24 says 'the left panel width is part 1's --size-left-panel'. Neither token table defines it; the two documents point at each other. The tablet Outline is 300 in 01 §3.2, 320 in 02 §16, and `--size-outline` 320 in 05 §19.
issues.fix: Define `--size-left-panel` 280 (≥1024) and `--size-left-panel-tablet` 320 once, in tokens.json and in 01 §20.2. Replace --size-outline-panel and --size-outline everywhere, and correct 01 §3.2's '300'.

issues.problem: Flow Designer component names drift between documents, and each claims the other owns the name. 01 §20.1 says it uses P2's 'IssuesChip' and 'ProblemsPanel'. 02 §4 and §24 say 'Part 1 §20.1 names this control IssuesButton' and call the panel 'ProblemsList'. Neither component table defines either. Outline rows are OutlineRow in 02 but OutlineItem plus BranchRow in 05 §10.7. The palette is StepPalette in 01 but AddStepSheet in 05. The meter is MicMeter in 03-pages/01 §7.9 but LevelMeter in 07. FlowHeader exists only in 05 §19. Full-screen mode is also contradictory: 01 §0, §3.1 and §19 say there is none, 02 §12 says the Problems bar is visible 'including full screen', overlay §18 'Resolves F-FLOW-034 via the compact bar', and 05 §10.3 specifies a floating bar in full screen at ≥1280.
issues.fix: Add a component registry to 04-flow-designer/01 §20.1 with name, owner section, props and variants (for example `IssuesChip`, `ProblemsPanel`, `FlowOutline` > `OutlineRow`, `StepPalette variant=panel|sheet`, `LevelMeter`, `FlowHeader`). Rename the other documents to match. Remove every full-screen reference from 02 §12, O §18 and 05 §10.3 (01 §21.3 X7 already decides 'No full-screen mode').

issues.problem: After publishing, the Publish button's state and focus contradict each other. 05 §10.8 says a clean draft hides Publish ('Publish hidden', 'no Publish button'). 01 §3.3, 02 §4 and §5, and 06 §7.3 and §19.B keep it aria-disabled with 'Nothing to publish', and 06 moves focus onto that button after a successful publish. If it's hidden, focus drops to `<body>`, which 06 §7.3 forbids. The published toast lasts 6 s in overlay §9 but 'stays until dismissed' in 05 §10.8.
issues.fix: In 05 §10.8, keep Publish visible and aria-disabled with 'Nothing to publish. Your draft matches Live v8.' at every width, including the phone state row. Make the publish toast 6 s (Roll back stays in the version menu) and cite overlay §9.

issues.problem: Some touch-target promises can't be met by the layouts other docs specify. Direction §6.5, foundations §14 and 06 §15.2 promise a 44 px socket hit area on coarse pointers, but 01 §6.1 clips the hit area to the 28 px answer row 'so neighbours never overlap', so it can never exceed 28 px. 06 §15.1 rule 2 says every target is 44×44 on coarse pointers, yet the short-height nav mode (05 §2.2, 00-app-shell-ia §3) uses 28 px items at ≥1024 wide and ≤800 tall, which includes coarse landscape tablets. The 06 §15.2 table also gives rail items no touch value ('—').
issues.fix: State the real rule. On `pointer: coarse`, answer rows grow to `--size-hit-touch` (44), and the socket target is the full-width row end, or connection goes through the tap-to-Connect to… path as the documented 2.5.8 equivalent. Apply short nav mode only under `(pointer: fine)`. Fill in the rail's touch row (44). Update direction §6.5, foundations §14 and 01 §6.1 to match.

issues.problem: The chrome-budget arithmetic treats the screen size as the viewport. 05 §3.4 ('1366×768 | 244 | 524 → 13 rows'), 00-app-shell-ia §4 and 03-leads §0 and §5.0 ('at least 12 at 1366×768') subtract chrome from 768. On a real 1366×768 Windows laptop, Chrome or Edge gives a viewport of about 1366×650. The `(max-height: 720px)` rule then always folds the Baseline (the direction's 'first signature' and the replacement for the wallet banner) into a chip on the reference device, and Leads shows about 10–11 rows, not 12–13.
issues.fix: Define test viewports as real inner sizes (1366×657, 1280×~610, 1536×730, 1920×~970), recompute the budgets in direction §6.1, 00-app-shell-ia §4, 03-leads §5.0 and 05 §3.4, and either lower the Baseline fold to `max-height: 600px` or state explicitly that BaselineChip is the primary status surface on 1366×768 and test it there.

issues.problem: The direction and its 'final specimen' still carry values that foundations §0 superseded. Direction §5 lists control #858D9C, live #16A34A, dark text #E9ECF1, Baseline #232935, a 16 px language mark (foundations uses 18 via --size-lang-mark), a size-adjusted Devanagari and 'Hanken is proportional'. Direction §8 gives `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *))` and `html.dark`, but the tokens use data-theme. 00-direction-specimen.html doesn't load tokens.css and hard-codes the old values, yet §0 of the direction calls it the 'Final specimen'.
issues.fix: Add a short errata box to direction §5 and §8 ('Values and theming mechanism are fixed in 01-foundations §0; where they differ, foundations wins') and correct the §8 code line to the data-theme variant. Label 00-direction-specimen.html 'non-normative: character only' in its header, or rebuild it on tokens.css.

issues.problem: `@custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme="dark"], [data-theme="dark"] *))` still matches inside a nested `[data-theme="light"]` island, which is the reason foundations §0 gives for choosing an attribute. It also never matches during the no-JS `prefers-color-scheme` fallback, so `dark:` utilities and token values can disagree. The file's comment says 'no var() here', but @theme contains `var(--font-hanken, …)`.
issues.fix: Use `@custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *):not(:where([data-theme=light], [data-theme=light] *)));` in build-tokens.mjs, or ban `dark:` in app code with lint (foundations §15.1 already says 'prefer token swaps'). Fix the comment.

issues.problem: Gate and popover elevation and radius differ between documents. Foundations §8 and direction §5 put gates at e3. Overlay §1 gives Popover e2 with radius-8 (radius-12 for the Call gate), and Leads §6.10 uses e2. Foundations §6 lists radius-6 for 'menus' but doesn't list popovers.
issues.fix: Add a Popover row (radius-8, e2) and a Gate popover row (radius-12, e3) to foundations §6 and §8, and make Leads §6.10 and overlay §1 cite them.

issues.problem: Duplicate size tokens invite misuse: static --size-tag (20) versus density-aware --tag-h (20/20/24), static --space-cell-px (12) versus density-aware --cell-px, and --size-hit-min versus core's --hit alias. --size-baseline stays 28 px below 1024 where no Baseline exists, so 06 §7.4's `main { scroll-padding-bottom: var(--size-baseline) }` adds dead padding on tablets and phones. 05 §20 also reports that html `scrollbar-gutter: stable` reserves an empty 15 px strip in the app shell.
issues.fix: Remove --size-tag and --space-cell-px, or mark them 'static reference, use --tag-h / --cell-px'. Set `--size-baseline: 0px` under `(max-width: 1023.98px)`. Move `scrollbar-gutter: stable` from html to the scrolling regions, as 05 §20 proposes, and update foundations §5.

issues.problem: Some values are off every scale: canvas controls 30 px tall (§9.1), fallback-row bottom radius 7 (§5.1), a 3 px inset test-run bar (§5.4), answer-row padding '0 20px 0 12px' as raw px, the password toggle at 26/38 px and segmented touch items at 38 px (core §3.3, §6.4). None are on the control-height (24/28/32/36/44), radius or border-width scales. Separately, the flow H1 is 'visually title-14', but foundations §2.3 and direction §5 say title-20 is the only H1 style. 05 §10.7 sets `maxZoom 1.5` while 01 §20.2 sets --zoom-max 2, and 01 §20.1 lists `snapToGrid` on FlowCanvas while 07 §15 sets `snapToGrid={false}`.
issues.fix: Snap the values to tokens: 32 (--control-h), radius 6 inner (concentric with 8 − 1 hairline, rounded to the scale), --bw-strong 2 px, `0 var(--space-20) 0 var(--space-12)`, and the password toggle at --control-h-sm. Record the flow H1 exception in foundations §2.3. Set one zoom maximum (2) and one snap rule (on release).

issues.problem: §12.1 gives both CallHeader and the TopBar call chip their own polite role=status wrapper. The Cockpit spec (§1.3, §4) routes call-state changes through the shell announcer, and 06 §12 allows only CallHeader's wrapper. On tablet and phone the same 'Call live' could be announced two or three times. §0.5 also says component aliases are 'declared per theme' in theme blocks, while foundations declares all aliases theme-agnostically on `:root, [data-theme], [data-surface]`.
issues.fix: Remove role=status from the TopBar chip; the state goes through the shell announcer only, as 06 §12.2 specifies. In §0.5, say the nav aliases are emitted by build-tokens.mjs from `component.nav` with per-mode values, the same mechanism as the semantic colours.

issues.problem: The setup track has six rows (an optional 'Teach your agent' first), while direction §6.1 defines five steps in a different order. The desktop mock shows three green ticks next to '2 of 5 done', which reads as a miscount, the kind of truth problem direction P1 is meant to prevent. The MoreSheet's current row uses the selection treatment (accent-soft) while sidebar and rail use the raised key. Foundations §5 says More lists 'all 12 destinations', but data-nav §1.8 and the direction say 'the remaining' destinations.
issues.fix: Either update direction §6.1 to six rows with an 'Optional · not counted' rule, or drop the row. Render optional completions with a neutral mark, not the success tick. Use the raised key for the current MoreSheet row. Correct foundations §5 to 'the 8 destinations not in the bar'.

issues.problem: The CI pair list misses pairs the specs create: status text on --surface-3 and --accent-soft (tags in selected rows); --accent-text on --accent-soft (links in selected rows); --control on the status softs (checkboxes inside notices); composited opacity cases; and the theme-split nav aliases and requested colours (--danger-hover, --qr-*). All the static ones pass today (for example, light danger-text on accent-soft is 5.83 and control on warning-soft is 3.33), but nothing guards them.
issues.fix: Add these pairs to `pairs` (status-text × [surface-3, accent-soft]; accent-text × SELECTED; control × SOFTS), add a `component` group that reads `component.*` from tokens.json, and add an `opacity` kind that composites the fg/bg pair at a given alpha over --canvas.

taste.verdict: Disciplined, usable and appropriately undecorated: no gradients, glass, AI glow or idle motion, real table hierarchy, excellent Call/Publish gates, and a Flow Designer that finally reads like a professional builder. But it does not yet read as Vaani. The shell is a close cousin of Linear (workspace switcher, 'Search or jump to', grouped nav with grey counts, raised active key, floating selection bar, view tabs with counts, keycap footer in the palette, near-black dark theme with periwinkle accent), Neel's hue (~230 deg) sits ~5 deg from Linear's indigo, and the three 'signatures' (Baseline, mono timecode gutter, answer rows) are Switchboard's status line, timecode gutter and port tabs renamed - the developer-console genre the taste judge already flagged. India-specific identity lives only in content on ~3 of 12 destinations; Leads, Billing, Settings, Knowledge and Analytics are interchangeable with any Tailwind/shadcn SaaS. Colour discipline is undermined by Neel carrying ~12 meanings (info = selection fill, charts, heatmap, talk strip, diff, variables), so Analytics renders solid blue and info notices look selected. Type/spacing are mostly sound but over-granular (22 type roles, 5 sizes between 12-16 px) and mono phone numbers/timers inside Hanken sentences add console flavour. The biggest handoff problem is consistency: every HTML mock re-implements components inline, so the Flow Designer, Baseline, StatusTag, LanguageMark, Call gate and phone nav are each drawn 2-6 different ways, and the 'final' specimen still ships superseded, contrast-failing values. Fix the two blockers (one shared component stylesheet + re-render; one canonical Flow Designer) before handoff; land the identity/accent majors before the HTML prototype.

issues.problem: No canonical visual reference. All 18 HTML mocks link only tokens.css/base.css and re-implement every component inline, so components drift between documents (see the Flow Designer, Baseline, Tag, LanguageMark, Call gate and phone-nav issues below). Worse, 00-direction-specimen.html (which this doc calls the final specimen) links no token file at all and still hard-codes the pre-foundations values that failed contrast: #858D9C control border (3 uses), #16A34A live dot, #666E7D dark control, and 0 uses of the corrected #7E8695 / #13923F / #6A7281 from 01-foundations section 0. A developer who copies CSS or colour-picks from the most prominent render reintroduces AA failures.
issues.fix: Generate one spec/components/components.css (Button, Tag/StatusTag, LanguageMark, PhoneText, Sidebar, Rail, TopBar, BottomBar, MoreSheet, PageHeader, Baseline, DataTable, Gate, StepNode + AnswerRow, TurnRow) next to tokens.css; relink every mock AND 00-direction-specimen.html to tokens.css + components.css and delete their inline component rules; re-render every PNG. Add a 'Canonical render' table to this doc mapping each signature component to exactly one PNG crop. Add a CI grep that fails when an HTML mock defines component classes inline or contains a hex value not present in tokens.css.

issues.problem: The flagship screen is drawn four different ways at 1440 and the text conflicts with itself. 04-flow-designer/01-canvas-and-nodes-desktop.png: chevron separators in the phase ruler, Outcome status line as a StatusTag with thumbs-up, labels on every edge, wallet chip in the header, play icon for Test. 02-config-validation-lifecycle-light.png: arrow separators, Outcome as plain 'Lead -> Interested', no edge labels, compact warning badges. 05-responsive-flow-1440.png: flask icon for Test, icon-only Tidy, green-tinted Outcome tile in the ruler, inspector answers as separate Label/Examples inputs, no wallet chip. 00-direction-specimen: silhouette glyphs in the ruler, examples right-aligned in answer rows, 'Publish anyway' checkbox instead of 'Publish with this warning'. Section 5.1 of this doc specifies a StatusTag on the Outcome line while direction 6.5 and 06-accessibility specify 'Lead -> Interested'. The phone Outline has two designs (04 mobile vs 05-responsive-flow-390) and tablet is read-only Review in 04 but full editing with Navigate/Arrange in 05.
issues.fix: Freeze one grammar and re-render 01, 02, 05-responsive-flow and the specimen from the shared node CSS: arrow-right (Lucide) between phase segments; Outcome status line as plain text 'Lead -> Interested' in meta-12 (the tile already carries tone - fewer chips on the canvas); edge labels only on hover, selection and long branch edges as section 7 says; play icon for Test (drop the flask, a lab/experiment cliche); Tidy labelled at >=1280; inspector answer editor = the 04-01 layout (handle, label + examples, 'Go to' select). Update section 5.1 here, direction 6.5 and 06-accessibility to the same sentence. Resolve tablet edit-vs-review once in 00-design-direction 6.5 and redraw whichever renders lose.

issues.problem: Identity is generic and too close to Linear. Section 1.5 claims five identity carriers, but visually: (1) the shell reproduces Linear's sidebar almost element for element (workspace switcher with up/down chevrons, search field under it, grouped nav with grey right-aligned counts, raised white active key on a grey sidebar, account at the bottom), plus Linear-style view tabs with counts, a floating centred selection bar and a palette footer of keycaps; (2) Neel #2B45C2 / dark #3752DA and #8FA3FF sit at HSL ~230 deg, about 5 deg from Linear's indigo #5E6AD2, and the dark text/focus colour reads periwinkle - the generic AI blue-violet the brief bans; (3) the Baseline in light mode is a black 28 px band - a VS Code status bar - and is the heaviest element on every screen, contradicting P7; (4) the mark is a letter V in an ink tile, i.e. a letter pseudo-icon. Devanagari, language marks and bilingual examples only appear on Cockpit, Call reports and the canvas.
issues.fix: (a) Re-key Neel toward actual indigo dye: darker and lower-chroma, hue ~215-220 deg, e.g. fill #1F4A94 (white 8.5:1), hover #183C7A, dark fill #2F62C0 (white 5.8:1), dark text/focus #8DB2EE (8.3:1 on #14171C); run check-contrast.mjs and compare side by side with Linear/Stripe screenshots before accepting. (b) Make the light-theme Baseline Neel-ink (~#17213F, --bl-text 10:1) instead of black, so the brand colour appears once at scale on every screen and the band stops reading as an IDE status bar. (c) Commission a real mark (thread/voice motif per the Sutradhar story) to replace the letter-V tile. (d) Rewrite section 1.5 to name which identity elements appear on every one of the 12 destinations, and drop the claim that the three signatures are new.

issues.problem: Neel is overloaded, breaking the direction's own rule 'if a screen looks blue, something is misusing it'. In tokens.css --info/--info-soft/--info-border ARE neel, and --accent-soft is documented as 'selected rows, the active phase segment, info notices', so an info notice is visually identical to a selection (see the 'No recording for this call' notice, the tablet 'Editing needs 1024 px' notice and the 'Session expired' notice). Neel is also --chart-1, all of --seq-1..5, --edge-active, the {{variable}} chips (04-01 section 5.1), the talk-strip and waveform agent lane, the compare-mode Added/Changed tint (identical to a selected node in 02-config-validation-lifecycle section 5), and the info-tone tags Streaming, Publishing, Scheduled, Indexing (plus 'Callback' in 00-app-shell-ia-laptop.png). Result: 04-call-reports-analytics renders as a solid royal-blue page. In dark, accent-soft #1B2340 over large areas (Home current step, selected rows) reads as a heavy navy slab.
issues.fix: Restrict Neel to primary fill, focus, selection, links, active nav icon and edge-active. Set --info-soft: var(--surface-2), --info-text: var(--text-2), --info-border: var(--border-strong) with the info icon in text-2.
