directions.name: Clear Path (guided clarity)
directions.essence: Every Vaani screen answers three questions in calm, plain language: where am I, what is true right now, and what is the one next step. Premium comes from effortlessness, not effects.

directions.name: Bolchaal (बोलचाल): voice-native identity
directions.essence: Conversation is the interface: a calm ink-on-khadi workspace where colour and motion belong only to the voice. Peacock marks what Vaani says and does, each call draws its own shape as it happens, and every language appears in its own script.

directions.name: Switchboard: the precision operator console
directions.essence: A calm operator's console: dense where you scan, quiet where you decide, and never wrong about what is live. Graphite chrome, a single Neel-blue accent for operator intent, and state colours only for real call and record state. Keyboard-first and density-controlled, with a Flow Designer that reads Trigger → Logic → Action → Outcome through node shape rather than colour. Every step that bills or goes live has an explicit commit: a pre-flight card or a Publish sheet.

strengths: Most distinctive and ownable of the three. Anek Latin (Ek Type, Mumbai) at wdth 112 / 600 for page titles and KPI numerals gives Vaani a typographic voice of its own. In the rendered Leads KPI strip (248 / 36 / 9 / 61%) and in 'Bolchaal बोलचाल' it looks premium, and it doesn't resemble Linear, Vercel or Stripe.

The colour story has a clear reason behind it. Khadi warm-neutral paper and ink (OKLCH hue 75, chroma < 0.01) with a single deep peacock (#006c85, white 6.0:1) avoids both the purple-blue AI glow and generic SaaS blue. It continues the existing --peacock token and the teal half of the logo, so the change reads as continuity.

The signature devices carry real data rather than decoration. Script chips (अ Hindi, த Tamil, অA Hinglish) are new, useful and visibly Indian. The conversation line in the Cockpit (agent vs caller lanes, 58/42 talk ratio, 1 interruption) replaces the idle orb (F-VIS-029). The voice meter doubles as the logo mark, which makes the brand system coherent.

The best-looking product surfaces in the set. Leads has a KPI strip, a language column of script chips, a Next step column, and a bulk bar that states cost and calling hours inline ('Est. ₹6 to ₹9 · Within calling hours · Review and call…'). The Cockpit shows 'Now at Ask about the site visit · step 2 of 8 · Open in flow' and a 'Captured so far 4 of 6' panel. Hindi turns are set in Devanagari.

The Flow Designer shape grammar actually reads in the render. Capsule Trigger and Outcome are clearly different from the rectangular work nodes. Answer tabs ('Interested / Later / Not now / No reply +') act as port labels. The missing No-reply path shows as a dashed amber tab, with 'Not connected' in the inspector. The header separates 'Live v6' from 'Draft · 3 changes' and 'Saved to draft 12:04'.

The warm near-black dark mode (#0f0e0c, warm off-white text) sets it apart from the ubiquitous cool blue-black dark UIs. It keeps Hanken Grotesk for the UI, as the audit recommends, so the marketing type system carries over.
weaknesses: The dark-mode primary is the weakest moment: a pale cyan #65bcd3 fill with ink label looks washed out and 'candy', and Publish, New lead and Call 2 leads lose their authority next to the deep teal of the light theme.
Draft is coloured as a warning. The amber 'Draft · 3 changes' chip sits next to the amber '1 warning' in the flow header, so two amber signals compete, and 'draft' is a normal state, not a warning.

Colour drift. The jamun plum Logic tile (#79466f / #cf95c1 in dark) sits close to the banned purple-AI trope, as the spec's own risk 6 admits. Ink, jamun, peacock and semantic tiles plus a 6-hue chart palette weaken the 'one accent' claim.

The pill count is high: status badges, filter chips, answer tabs, capsules and the call-state pill are all fully round, and cards and panels use 12 px radii. Together these soften the product towards consumer and away from precise professional tooling.
Mini conversation lines in every Leads row add visual texture to a dense table. They also depend on diarisation data that may not exist, so they could render empty, or tempt someone to fake them.
Three Latin-bearing families (Anek, Hanken, JetBrains Mono) plus Anek Indic scripts. Anek-wide titles next to Hanken UI could look mismatched if the roles leak beyond the 5 locked tokens.

The Flow Designer is less of a 'pro instrument' than Switchboard's. It has no phase counts spine and no Problems bar in the render, the ports are small dots under the pills, and the top-down layout will sprawl sideways with 4 or more branches. The breakpoints section is text cards only, with no rendered tablet or laptop layout.

strengths: The strictest colour discipline of the three: graphite chrome, one Neel accent for operator intent, and green, amber and red only for real call or record state. Node types differ by shape and glyph, not hue, which removes the 1.48–2.34:1 coloured titles (F-FLOW-007).

The most professional Flow Designer render. Left-to-right phases, a phase spine with counts (Trigger 2 → Logic 2 → Action 5 → Outcome 5), and labelled port rows with bilingual example utterances ('Yes · haan, zaroor', 'Later · baad mein', 'No reply · after 6 s'). Dashed lines are reserved for fallback, a Problems bar carries 'Go to step', and the header shows 'Draft · from v7 / Live v7 / Publish v8…'. It reads like a serious circuit or workflow editor.

The timecode-gutter transcript is broadcast-grade: fixed mm:ss gutter, speaker, a language tag, and a Q1 step chip linking back to the node. The same row anatomy is reused across Cockpit, Reports, Rep console and Test.

The status line is a functional, ownable shell element. The 28 px ink bar in light mode computes live flow, number readiness, wallet (linking to Billing) and calls in progress, and replaces both the 42 px banner and the fake 'SYS: ONLINE'.

Typographic rigour: IBM Plex Sans, Mono and Devanagari form one superfamily with a designed Devanagari companion and default tabular figures. The page title is a restrained 20/600, and the rules for mono and uppercase are explicit.

Real density control (40 px Standard, 32 px Compact). The Leads render fits about 10 rows with a crisp pre-flight card ('Nothing dials until you start. Checked just now.', DND, calling hours, cost, wallet).
weaknesses: Weak distinctiveness. IBM Plex, cool graphite, a royal-blue accent, ⌘K and keycaps everywhere put it in the developer-console genre (Linear/Raycast family). Neel #2C4BD1 reads as standard SaaS blue in the renders, not as indigo, and Plex carries an IBM/Carbon association.
It overrides the audit's 'keep Hanken Grotesk' recommendation, which forces a marketing re-set for a typeface that adds little identity.

Heavy use of small boxed mono tokens: HI/EN tags, Q1/T1/KB chips, keycaps inside primary buttons ('New lead N', 'Start 3 calls ⌘↵'), caps-11 'TRIGGER/ACTION/OUTCOME' labels and {{vars}}. Together they read as a softened version of the HUD dialect the audit wants retired, and they add chatter to transcripts and buttons.

The shape grammar is too subtle in the render. The half-round Trigger and Outcome edges read as ordinary rounded corners, the 3 px terminal bar is effectively invisible, and at a glance every node is the same white card.
Dark mode is competent but generic graphite. The status line, its signature, nearly disappears in dark: #1A1E24 on a #0D0F13 background loses the 'lamp row' contrast it has in light.
The breakpoints section renders empty wireframe boxes, so tablet and laptop layouts are not shown. On mobile the status-line specimen clips horizontally at 375 px.

strengths: The clearest statement of the draft/live split. A live strip under the flow header reads 'v7 is answering calls on +91 ••••• 2210 since 12 Sep. Callers keep hearing v7 until you publish this draft.' and offers 'Compare with live'.

Strong functional signatures. The Readiness path reuses one component for setup ('Get your first call live', 3 of 5), the sidebar 'Finish setup 4 of 5', and the pre-call check. That check includes 'called 22 hours ago · Include' for repeat-call protection, and a status line grammar of state badge + sentence + one action.
The Cockpit call-state stepper (Dialling → Ringing → Live → Wrap-up) with timestamps, and a 'Now in the flow' mini-path that ties the call to the canvas.
Keeps Hanken Grotesk and the marketing type system. The copy is plain-language and sentence case throughout, and the component state matrix is complete and legible.
weaknesses: The least distinctive of the three. Hanken, cool mineral grey, teal, numbered-circle principle cards with halo rings and vertical check-circle steppers add up to a generic modern SaaS onboarding look, with nothing ownable beyond the teal, which Bolchaal uses better.

Flow stage tiles bring in indigo and violet: When #3E4BC0 on #EDEFFC, Check #7F3E9C on #F5ECF8, and #9AA6FF / #D59BEA in dark. These pastel lavender and pink tiles drift towards the banned purple-blue AI palette.

The Flow Designer is visually the weakest. Nodes are small, text is about 12 px, thin curved edges cross a lot of empty canvas, and it feels closer to a consumer automation tool than a professional builder. Renaming to When/Check/Do/End also moves away from the brief's Trigger → Logic → Action → Outcome vocabulary.
Softer geometry (8/12/16 radii, halo markers, three shadow levels, Comfortable 52 px default) reads as friendly rather than premium and precise.
Dark mode is generic cool teal-black with a pale-cyan primary (#5BC3D6 with ink label), plus lavender trigger tiles. The mobile specimen header wraps badly into three columns.

grafts: From operator: the Flow Designer's phase spine with counts and click-to-filter (Trigger 2 → Logic 2 → Action 5 → Outcome 5), placed above the canvas in place of Bolchaal's static legend chip.

From operator: Logic nodes list outputs as labelled port rows with example utterances ('Yes · haan, zaroor', 'Later · baad mein', 'No reply · after 6 s'), each with its own 10 px socket and 24 px hit area. The fallback row is mandatory and is the only dashed edge. This replaces Bolchaal's small dots under pills.

From operator: the bottom Problems bar ('1 warning · Book site visit: WhatsApp template pending approval · Go to step') plus Outline and Test panel toggles, and the version-explicit header ('Draft · from v7', 'Live v7', 'Publish v8…').

From operator: the rule that colour means state and shape means type. Drop the jamun plum Logic tile and tell categories apart by capsule versus rectangle plus a glyph, with neutral tiles. Keep peacock for selection, the test trace and the agent only.

From operator: the timecode-gutter row anatomy. Add the Q1 step chip that links a transcript turn to its node, and the knowledge-source note ('KB · price-sheet.pdf'). Reuse the same row in Cockpit, Call reports, Rep console and flow Test.

From operator: the ambient status line concept (live flow, number readiness, wallet linking to Billing, calls in progress, computed only), adapted to Bolchaal's warm ink tile. Or at minimum its low-wallet and 'No calling number · Finish setup (2 of 4)' states in the sidebar wallet card.
From operator: a real density setting (Standard 40 / Compact 32 rows for data surfaces only), toggled with ⇧D, so operators get about 12–16 rows at 1440×900.

From clarity: the live strip under the flow header ('v7 is answering calls on +91 ••••• 2210 since 12 Sep. Callers keep hearing v7 until you publish this draft · Compare with live'). It is the most explicit fix for F-FLOW-001.

From clarity: the Readiness path as one component for Home setup, the sidebar 'Finish setup 4 of 5', the pre-call check with the repeat-call guard ('called 22 hours ago · Include'), and the Publish checklist.
From clarity: the Cockpit call-state stepper (Dialling → Ringing → Live → Wrap-up with timestamps) and the 'Now in the flow' mini-path under the conversation line.
must_fix: Dark-mode accent: stop using pale cyan #65bcd3 as the primary button fill with ink text. Use a deeper mid-peacock fill (verify the label at ≥4.5:1) and keep the light cyan only for links, focus, the agent lane and text on dark, so primary actions keep their weight in dark.
Draft must not be amber. Show 'Draft · 3 changes' as a neutral or accent-soft chip, and reserve amber for warnings, ringing and low balance, so the flow header shows only one amber signal.
Remove the purple adjacency: no jamun or plum or violet anywhere in chrome or flow tiles (also check the chart 'Jamun' and 'Indigo' series), in line with the brief's ban on generic AI palettes.

Reduce pill shapes. Keep full-round only for status badges and trigger and outcome capsules. Filter chips and answer port tabs become 6 px rectangles, and panel radii stay at 8 px, so the product reads as precise tooling rather than consumer.

Lock Anek to page title, KPI and display tokens with a lint rule. Never use it for anything that ticks, since it has no guaranteed tabular figures. Show a side-by-side of an Anek 24 px H1 over Hanken 13–14 px table text in both themes to prove the pairing holds.
Leads conversation-line column: hide it by default or move it to Call reports, and never render it without real diarised turn data. Tables should stay calm and scannable.

Flow Designer must render the full lifecycle visually: a Publish sheet with validation, a diff and where the flow goes live; the 'Couldn't save · Retry' state; Publish blocked with an inline reason when there are errors; and keyboard focus on a node and a port. These are the critical audit issues F-FLOW-001/003/004 and F-A11Y-001.

Render the breakpoints instead of describing them. Show designed tablet (768–1023) and laptop (1024–1439) layouts for the shell, Leads and the Flow Designer, plus the mobile More sheet reaching all 12 sections (F-RWD-001), and make sure no specimen element clips at 320–375 px.

Keep mono strictly to phone numbers, timers, IDs, {{variables}} and keycaps. Don't put keycaps inside primary button labels, and don't bring back the caps-tracked HUD labels, so the audit's five dialects collapse to one.

Verify every text and control pair in both themes after the changes above, including text-3 on surface-2, the lane-human track at ≥3:1 and edge contrast on the dark canvas. Fixing muted #7A8397 and black-on-blue (F-A11Y-008/009) is non-negotiable.

strengths: Its Flow Designer is the best for the real 26–35-node flows (03C Flow A/B). Flows read left to right. A 40 px phase spine counts steps per phase, and clicking a phase dims the others. The 48 px single header, the sidebar collapsing to a 56 px rail and the palette as a popover give the canvas about 75% of the viewport (F-FLOW-022). It has zoom level-of-detail with 12 px counter-scaled labels (F-FLOW-008), frames, Cmd/Ctrl+F find, an Outline, ELK Tidy that respects frames, and a minimap that hides below 1280 px.

Trigger → Logic → Action → Outcome is explicit. The canonical words appear in the palette, spine, caps labels, outline and validator, and the render (operator-light/dark) reads correctly. The phase is carried by shape: a half-round entry edge for Trigger, port rows for Logic, a terminal bar for Outcome. Each Outcome node writes the lead status ('Lead → Interested'), which closes the missing outcome taxonomy.

Port tabs are named output rows with Hinglish examples ('Yes · haan, zaroor', 'No reply · after 6 s'). Each has a 24 px socket and a mandatory dashed fallback. Branch meaning no longer depends on handle position or colour (F-FLOW-020, F-FLOW-011), and the C 'Connect to…' listbox plus Enter/A/arrow keys make the canvas keyboard-operable (F-A11Y-001).

The lifecycle is the most complete of the three. It has a Live v7 chip next to 'Draft · from v7', a save-state machine that ignores hydration and fitView (F-QA-002), If-Match with 409 on conflict, and a flush on pagehide. A Publish sheet shows validation, a diff and where the flow goes live. 'Restore as draft' never overwrites Live, and AI draft works as a diff to apply to the draft (F-FLOW-001/003/004/031).

A 28 px computed status line (live flow, number readiness, wallet → /billing#wallet, calls in progress) replaces the 42 px banner and the fake SYS: ONLINE (F-UX-002, F-UX-018, F-UX-028). Disabled Place call shows its reason inline ('Wallet is ₹0. Top up in Billing').

The pre-flight card covers every dialling path: Leads row, bulk, Cockpit and 'Call me with this draft'. It shows flow and version, voice, calling hours, DND 'n of n clear', a rupee estimate and wallet. C never dials, and single-key shortcuts can be switched off (F-UX-013, F-A11Y-004).

IA stays continuous: it keeps the names Cockpit, Flows, Leads and Call reports, with one name per destination and four sidebar groups. Settings gets a grouped sub-nav, and phones get a 5-tab bar plus a More sheet that reaches all 12 sections (F-RWD-001).

Density fits operators. Standard 40 px and Compact 32 px rows show about 12 to 16 leads at 1440x900, against 7 today (F-VIS-009). Touch automatically switches to 48/44 px. The Cockpit wrap-up has 'Save and next (N)' for working through a list.
weaknesses: Onboarding for SMB first-timers is thin. The only setup tracker is 'Finish setup (2 of 4)' in the status line and on the Cockpit. There is no Home or Get-started route, no template gallery for a first flow, and on tablet and phone the status line collapses to a '● ₹2,340' chip, so setup progress disappears exactly where F-UX-006 and F-UX-001 bite.

The phone outline is grouped by phase (every Logic step together, every Action together), so it loses the branch paths. On operator-mobile you cannot tell where 'Yes' leads, which defeats review on phone and tablet.

Logic and Action nodes are both plain rectangles. At the lowest zoom level ('phase-shaped blocks') the two are nearly indistinguishable, and shape plus 16 px glyphs carry the whole phase distinction on a monochrome canvas.
Uppercase 11 px table headers break the 12 px floor the other two keep (36% of text is under 12 px today, F-VIS-002).
The spec never says whether the status line (28 px) shows inside the Flow Designer, where it would stack with the 32 px Problems bar and cut into the claimed 75% canvas.
Billing is a list of tab names only (Wallet · Usage · Plans · Invoices · Autopay). The UPI top-up sheet, presets, autopay and per-call usage are not specified.
The Risks section lets admins switch off the pre-flight for small batches. That reopens F-UX-013 unless it is tightly bounded.
Switching from the Hanken Grotesk the audit recommends to IBM Plex adds migration cost and a marketing re-set, with no usability gain beyond Devanagari parity (Noto or Anek could deliver that).

strengths: It has the strongest onboarding and truthful setup. Home becomes the default route with a 'Get your first call live' readiness path: choose a flow, add a number, add money, call yourself, then import leads or connect inbound. It says live only after a connected test call. A persistent sidebar card reads 'Finish setup · 4 of 5 · Next: invite team' (F-UX-006, F-UX-001, J1).

The readiness popover is the best pre-call check of the three. Blocking checks (no live flow, unverified number, wallet, outside hours) disable the button and say why. Advisory checks (recently called 22 h ago is auto-skipped with an Include link, DND, language mismatch) adjust the batch. Cost is a range ('2 calls · about 2 to 4 min · ₹10 to ₹20'), batches land in Live calls › Scheduled with Pause and Cancel, and every request carries an idempotency key.

The live strip under the flow header says in plain language what callers hear: 'Live v7 is answering calls on +91 ••••• 2210 since 12 Sep. Callers keep hearing v7 until you publish this draft' with Compare. It is the clearest single fix for the draft/live confusion.
In the inspector, each answer under 'Answers to listen for' has a 'Go to [step ▾]' select, so users can wire a flow without dragging. That suits both novices and screen-reader users (A8, F-A11Y-001).
New flows open a sheet with a template gallery drawn as mini strips, plus a 'Describe it' AI draft onto a new draft. Every template passes validation (F-FLOW-013, F-FLOW-031).
Publish readiness includes 'test call on this draft' (advisory, skippable with a recorded reason), and test results feed it. That ties testing to publishing.

The status-line grammar ([badge] + sentence + meta + one action) is applied across Knowledge indexing, Meeting rooms, Rep desk and save failures, and every data view ships empty, filtered-empty, loading, error and no-permission states.

The phone flow outline reads as sentences ('Yes: book a site visit, then Visit booked'), and all 12 destinations are reachable through More. The wallet low-balance status line appears only where calling is blocked, and 'Top up…' opens the top-up sheet directly.
weaknesses: The Flow Designer renames the brief's required Trigger → Logic → Action → Outcome as When → Check → Do → End, so the brief's own vocabulary never appears in the product.

The large-flow tooling is weakest here. There is no zoom level-of-detail (F-FLOW-008 is not addressed), no frames or groups, and no canvas find (the palette's 'Find a step…' is add-step search). A 256 px palette is pinned at 1440 alongside a 328–360 px inspector, leaving the canvas 55–60%. Top-down layout with 11–12 px node text at 86% zoom will not scale to 26–35 nodes.
It adds indigo (When) and plum (Check) stage hues. That stretches the one-accent rule and edges toward the purple/indigo 'AI' palette the brief warns against.
Comfortable 52 px rows by default favour newcomers over the operators who live in Leads and Call history all day.

Renaming Cockpit to Live calls, Call Reports to Call history and Rep Console to Rep desk, and adding Home, costs existing users their muscle memory and breaks docs. Redirects and 'formerly' search entries only soften it.
'Undo publish' for 10 minutes is semantically unsafe once calls have already run on v8. Restoring the previous version is honest; undo is not.
End call asks for confirmation during a live call, which slows an urgent hang-up.
The mobile specimen render duplicates the page at the end (a stitching artifact), so phone review evidence is noisier than for the other two.

strengths: The Flow Designer is solid and friendly to newcomers. It uses the exact Trigger → Logic → Action → Outcome words, with a legend chip, numbered palette groups, capsules for entry and exit, rectangles for work, and category colour only in 24 px tiles. Its header shows the Live v6 and 'Draft · 3 changes' badges and a save chip, and Publish is disabled with the reason inline.

The inspector names unfinished wiring well. An amber 'No reply · Not connected' row comes with a fix hint, answers show their targets ('Later → Schedule callback'), and warnings go through an explicit 'Publish with 1 warning'.

The conversation line (two lanes for talk ratio, turns and interruptions, with a now-marker) turns the live Cockpit card and the Call-reports recording scrubber into something you can read and seek by keyboard. It is useful where audio exists.
The phone flow outline is nested by branch ('If Interested → Book site visit → Visit booked') with issue badges. It is the best mobile review view of the three.
At 1440 px and up, the Cockpit adds a Calls column (Live now, Up next, Recent) for supervisors watching several concurrent calls.

Blocking notices appear as role=status only on pages whose primary task is blocked. A sidebar wallet card shows balance and runway, with 'Top up in Billing' linking to /billing#top-up (F-UX-002, F-UX-028).
weaknesses: Leads keeps a KPI strip above the table, leaving about 230 px of chrome (Switchboard's is 148 px). On phones the render shows only 3 leads per screen, against the spec's own claim of at least 5 (F-VIS-009).
Mini conversation lines in the Leads 'Last call' column add visual noise with little decision value, and they depend on diarisation data the risks section admits may not exist.

Script-chip glyphs at 12 px read poorly (अA renders like '3IA' in the specimen), and a user who reads Tamil will not recognise a Telugu or Bengali glyph key. The language name has to carry the meaning anyway.
The spec breaks its own accent rule: it says the accent is never used for status, yet 'Interested' is an accent badge and accent port pills.

Its large-flow tooling is weaker than Switchboard's. It has no frames or grouping, and top-to-bottom layout with horizontal pill ports widens Logic nodes to 360 px. With the 216 px palette pinned plus a 328 px inspector at 1440, 26–35-node flows go wide and sparse.
Onboarding is only an Account-group 'Setup · 3 of 5' item plus a Cockpit card, less guided than Clear Path's Home readiness path.

Its identity rests on two Latin faces (Anek display plus Hanken UI), warm khadi neutrals and a plum Logic tile. That adds brand risk and lint burden without improving usability, and the plum sits near the 'purple AI' trope.

Add a persistent sidebar 'Finish setup · n of 5 · Next: …' card that also appears in the phone More sheet and the tablet nav sheet. It replaces Switchboard's status-line-only 'Finish setup (2 of 4)'.

From Clear Path: rebuild Switchboard's pre-flight card on the readiness-popover logic. Blocking checks (no live flow, unverified number, wallet below minimum, outside calling hours) disable Start and state the reason. Advisory checks (called in the last 24 h, auto-skipped with an Include link; DND; language mismatch) adjust the batch. From Clear Path: the live-strip sentence. When the draft differs from Live, show one line under the 48 px header, 'Live v7 is answering calls on +91 ••••2210 since 12 Sep. From Clear Path: in Switchboard's Configure tab, give each answer row a 'Go to [step ▾]' select, so users can wire and rewire a step without dragging. It is the mouse-friendly counterpart to the C 'Connect to…' listbox.

From Clear Path: a New flow sheet with a template gallery (Lead qualification, Site visit, EMI reminder, COD confirmation, Appointment, Support FAQ), each drawn as a mini Trigger → Logic → Action → Outcome strip, plus 'Describe it' for an AI draft onto a new draft. From Clear Path: add an advisory 'Test call placed on this draft' check to the Publish sheet (skippable with a recorded reason). The result of the Test panel feeds it.

From Clear Path: keep Trigger, Logic, Action and Outcome as the canonical phase names, but add a plain-language one-liner under each palette group heading (Trigger: when a call starts; Logic: listen and decide; Action: do something for the caller; Outcome: how the call ended). First-timers get the meaning without losing the brief's vocabulary.

From Clear Path: the per-view state matrix (empty, filtered-to-nothing, loading, error with Retry, and no-permission naming the admin) for every data view. Use the status-line grammar ([badge] + sentence + meta + one action) for Knowledge indexing, Meetings, Rep console availability and save failures.
From Bolchaal: the phone and tablet Outline nested by branch ('If Yes → Book site visit → Visit booked', with issue badges and Test), replacing Switchboard's grouping by phase.

From Bolchaal: the two-lane conversation line in the Cockpit live card and as the keyboard-seekable recording scrubber in the Call reports detail sheet (role=slider, ±5 s). Only there, never in the Leads table, and hidden when there is no per-turn data.
From Bolchaal: the Cockpit ≥1440 'Calls' column (Live now, Up next, Recent) in place of the header switcher, for supervisors with several concurrent calls.
From Bolchaal: an explicit 'Publish with 1 warning' button label, and unconnected required ports (including No reply) shown as an amber 'Not connected' row in the inspector with a one-line fix hint.

From Bolchaal: show the wallet as runway ('₹142.50 · about 23 minutes' or 'about 10 calls') wherever the wallet appears, computed from the real rate. That covers the status line, the phone status chip and the Billing header.
must_fix: Onboarding must exist at every breakpoint. Provide a persistent, tracked setup route that fixes the circular org/team creation (F-UX-001). It never says 'live' or 'ready' until number, wallet, a published flow and a connected test call all check out (F-UX-006), and it stays visible on tablet and phone, not only in the desktop status line.

Specify Billing as a real page, not tab names. The Wallet tab needs a UPI top-up sheet (keep the ₹100/500/1000 presets, validate custom amounts) and a balance with runway. Usage must count calls, not legs (F-QA-006), Invoices must be listed, and Autopay needs states. Every 'Top up' link anywhere opens that top-up sheet directly (F-UX-002, F-QA-004).

Large-flow editing needs the full toolset: zoom level-of-detail with labels never below 12 px on screen (F-FLOW-008); frames that collapse; canvas find that is separate from add-step search; multi-select with a count and a bulk bar (move, frame, delete with undo); Tidy that respects frames; and a restored saved viewport. Validate the whole set against the real 26- and 35-node flows.

Phase recognition cannot rely on silhouette alone at low zoom. Logic and Action are both rectangles, so keep the phase glyph (and label) visible in the compact and block levels of detail, and give the four glyphs distinct neutral treatments. Do not bring back category hue on node frames.

The phone and tablet flow Outline must show branch paths and targets, issues, the Live and Draft versions, and Test. Editing structure below 1024 px stays out of scope, but Publish must never be clipped (F-RWD-003).

Define the chrome stacking in the Flow Designer. Either hide the 28 px status line there or merge its live-flow and wallet facts into the 48 px header, so it does not stack with the 32 px Problems bar and eat the canvas.
The text floor is 12 px everywhere, including table column headers. Drop Switchboard's 11 px uppercase caps or raise it to 12 px.

No setting, including an admin one, may skip the pre-flight for billable calls. The cost line and blocking checks always show. Offer at most a remembered 'tested today' state and one-keystroke confirm (C then ⌘/Ctrl+Enter).

Publish semantics must be explicit. State which numbers, campaigns and Cockpit default use the flow (resolve 'active flow' per trigger, F-FLOW-014). Offer 'Restore v7 as draft/publish', never an 'undo publish' that implies calls already made on v8 can be reversed.

Sequence the backend before the visuals: draft/published revisions with If-Match, server-side validation returning the same rule set, two-leg de-duplication, server pagination for Call reports (F-QA-005) and whole-pipeline view counts. Until each exists, its UI state must be hidden rather than simulated.
Migrate the existing flows to left-to-right as an opt-in 'Re-layout' draft that must be published, never a rewrite of live flows.
The phone status chip must separate call state from wallet state. The '● ₹2,340' chip must not imply a live call, and a blocked wallet must also appear inline on the phone's Call actions.

Extend the spec beyond Leads, Cockpit and Flows with page templates for the Call reports detail sheet (keyboard-openable rows, focus-managed, F-A11Y-002), Knowledge indexing states, Assistant approvals (Personal Agent autonomy levels), Meetings, Personal agents, Rep console and Settings › Organization & team.

Settle the default typeface. Unless Plex's Devanagari parity is demonstrated in user testing, keep Hanken Grotesk (the audit's recommendation and the marketing face) with a matched Devanagari companion, to avoid a two-brand migration.

strengths: Most complete, directly implementable token system. It has a 12-step graphite ramp and role tokens (bg/surface/surface-2/3, border/border-strong/control, text/2/3/disabled, accent/hover/soft/focus/on-accent, success/warning/danger soft+solid pairs, live, status line), a named z-scale (0-70, no 9999, fixes F-QA-038), 3 motion tokens plus one easing, a 4px spacing scale and a Tailwind v4 @theme excerpt. It also includes a one-to-one migration table from today's 32 variables (--saffron to --accent, --peacock retired, --text-muted #7a8397 to --text-3 #5F6878, glass/grid/noise/glow deleted).

I recomputed every contrast pair and they are exact: text-3 5.62 on surface and 4.70 on surface-3, white on accent 6.92 light and 5.37 dark, --control 3.34 (light) and 3.50 (dark) for WCAG 1.4.11, focus 6.92 and 8.08. It is the only direction with no failing text pair in either theme. It fixes F-A11Y-008 and F-A11Y-009 and gives every input a boundary of at least 3:1, where the audit found none.

Lowest colour migration. The cool graphite ramp continues today's #111725 ink and #E1E6EF hairlines. Neel #2C4BD1 sits next to the shipped #2F5FE0, and one hue in both themes fixes F-VIS-004/DESIGN-SYSTEM-03 without re-branding marketing colours.

The strongest density model of the three. It uses real tokens (--row, --ctl, --cell-x) with Standard 40/32, Compact 32/28 and Touch 48/44, applied automatically on `pointer: coarse`. Density covers data surfaces only, forms stay calm, and data text has a 13px floor. This fits the ops-team users and F-VIS-009.

Signature elements with low data dependency. The status line uses data the client already has (live flow, number readiness, wallet, calls in progress) and replaces the 42px banner and fake SYS: ONLINE (F-UX-018, F-UX-028). The timecode gutter uses the existing transcript timestamps. Port tabs are standard React Flow multi-handle custom nodes.

The Flow Designer is the most engineered: shape+glyph+phase label instead of colour (colour-blind-safe, fixes the 1.48-2.34:1 node titles in F-FLOW-007), 10px sockets with 24px hit areas, a mandatory fallback row as the only dashed edge, zoom level-of-detail with labels counter-scaled to 12px (F-FLOW-008), a save-state machine that ignores hydration/fitView events plus If-Match/409 (F-QA-002, F-FLOW-003), a Publish sheet with validation and diff, a server 422 validator, and a full keyboard map plus an Outline editor (F-A11Y-001).

Motion is minimal and implementable: 90/140/200ms, transform and opacity only, no transition:all. The only perpetual motion is the live dot and real audio meters, and both stop under reduced motion (F-A11Y-022).
The specimen is performance-clean: no backdrop-filter and no decorative gradients (only the canvas dot grid).
weaknesses: The swap from Hanken Grotesk to IBM Plex is the largest single migration cost. It contradicts the audit's 'keep Hanken' strength, forces a marketing re-set, and brings an IBM/Carbon association that works against an 'own identity'. The specimen loads 4 Plex Sans faces (including an italic), 2 Plex Mono and 3 Plex Sans Devanagari. The spec itself admits the system works unchanged on Hanken.
The icon-only 56px rail covers all of 1024-1439. That includes 1280-1439, where there is room for a labelled sidebar. The audit criticised icon-only nav (F-UX-007, DESIGN-SYSTEM-20).

Keyboard focus and selection look almost identical: both are a 2px #2C4BD1 outline in light mode on canvas nodes, and accent bars on table rows. Keyboard users cannot tell 'where I am' from 'what is selected'.

It never states the Tailwind v4 dark-variant fix (`@custom-variant dark`), so the OS-media dark: leak in DESIGN-SYSTEM-11/F-VIS-021 remains. The @theme names produce awkward utilities (`text-text-3`). Tokens are duplicated in both `:root.dark` and a prefers-color-scheme block with no single source.
The sub-12px exceptions are not fully accounted for: caps-11 headers, 11px mono keycaps and 11px phone bottom-bar labels in the specimen.

The dark status line (#1A1E24) is only 1.15:1 against the dark bg, so it depends on a hairline to read as a band. In light mode the ink bar is heavy, and 28px of permanent chrome is costly on 1366x768 laptops.
The status line is `role=contentinfo` with polite announcements. Wallet decrements and call timers would spam screen readers unless they are explicitly excluded.
Left-to-right default layout needs a one-time re-layout of the 16 existing top-down flows. The cost estimate ('≈ ₹11') looks more precise than it is.

strengths: Lowest typography migration and weight. It keeps the already-shipped Hanken Grotesk and JetBrains Mono (the audit strength), adds only Noto Sans Devanagari through unicode-range, and retires 9 registrations. This is the lightest font payload of the three.

Cleanest Tailwind v4 wiring. Theme values live in plain CSS variables and are mapped into @theme as `--color-fg/-fg-2/-fg-3`, which avoids `text-text-3`. It includes shadow tokens, a lint rule banning arbitrary values and raw palette classes, Radix or React Aria primitives, TanStack Table, and an explicit component build order (Button, Field, Badge, StatusLine, ReadinessPath, PageHeader, AppShell, DataTable, Sheet, flow node set).

The Readiness path is one component with page/popover/inline/horizontal variants, reused for setup (F-UX-006), the pre-call and bulk-call check (F-UX-013), Publish, and the call-state and telephony steppers. This is excellent systemisation that reuses the audit's best existing pattern.

Contrast is honest and it flags its own failing pair (text-3 on surface-3 is 4.49 and marked 'never'). Values verified: text-3 5.15 on canvas, white on peacock 6.16, border-strong 3.31 (light) and 3.16 (dark).
Keyboard and screen-reader wiring is simple to build. The inspector's 'Answers to listen for → Go to [select]' list complements the Outline view and the canvas keyboard model.
Strong state coverage: empty, filtered, loading (200ms delay), error, no-permission and import preview states for Leads, plus an Undo-publish toast and advisory vs blocking checks.
weaknesses: Token hygiene is loose: r-xs is 5px (off the 4px grid), the segmented control is 7-inside-9, and field gaps are '16-18 px'. These reintroduce the off-grid values the audit wants gone (DESIGN-SYSTEM-15).
Comfortable is the default (52px rows, 36px controls). That is less dense for ops teams, and there is no touch-density token.

The IA migration cost is high. It renames destinations (Live calls, Call history, Rep desk, Call flows) and adds a new Home route, which means redirects, docs and retraining. It also replaces the brief's required Trigger → Logic → Action → Outcome vocabulary with When/Check/Do/End.

The accent is a brand change (peacock replaces the app blue and the marketing violet, so the logo and marketing must move). Peacock #0A6A84 and success #1B7A3F are only 1.15:1 apart in luminance with a 48° hue gap, which is a colour-vision-deficiency risk.
Stage tiles add indigo #3E4BC0 and plum, stretching the one-accent rule. The indigo drifts towards the generic blue-violet AI palette.
There is no zoom level-of-detail. The 86% canvas in the specimen renders node body text at about 11px on screen (F-FLOW-008 is not addressed).

Node keyboard focus is specified as 'the same outline as selected'. The 37px live strip under the header eats canvas height. The mobile filter chip clips ('Language Hindi, Engli…'). The dark-variant fix is missing.

strengths: The most distinctive identity with a real Indian anchor, applied with restraint. Script chips, and `lang` on every transcript turn with Devanagari at line-height 1.7, are genuinely useful for Hindi/English users.
The token appendix is the only one that explicitly fixes the Tailwind dark variant (`@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *))`, F-VIS-021) and names one theme mechanism.

Contrast is largely verified: text-3 5.12 on canvas, white on peacock 6.03, dark on-accent 8.32, border-control 3.25 and 3.27, edges 3.1. It pairs icon plus label for state and uses one red instead of four.
It keeps a labelled sidebar down to 1280, with the rail only at 1024-1279, and specifies a 200%-zoom behaviour. Blocking notices appear only on pages whose primary task is blocked (role=status).
Zoom level-of-detail with counter-scaled labels, 24px port hit areas and a keyboard map on the canvas.
weaknesses: Highest migration cost. The warm 'khadi' ramp replaces the entire cool neutral ramp (every surface, border and text colour changes, with a beige-drift risk on low-end screens). Peacock replaces the brand hue, capsules and pills add a new shape language, and the typography becomes 4 families (Anek Latin display with a wdth axis, Hanken, JetBrains Mono, Anek Devanagari, plus lazily loaded Anek Tamil/Telugu/Bangla).
Two Latin sans faces. Anek lacks guaranteed tabular figures, and the specimen loads the full wdth 75-125 and wght 400-700 axes for both Anek families, far more than the 2 instances it uses.

The signature elements depend on data that may not exist: diarised turn start and end times for the conversation line, client-side audio RMS for the voice meter (carrier calls may not expose it), and per-turn language ID for script chips. A lot of the identity may have to be hidden in production.

Peacock is overloaded. It means primary, focus, selection, the agent lane and the Action category tile, so a selected Action node and an unselected one differ only subtly. Jamun (plum) for Logic sits near the purple-AI trope.
Unflagged contrast gaps: text-3 on surface-3 is 4.45 (surface-3 is the neutral badge fill), and the warning solid #e4a339 is 2.19:1 on white when used as a standalone indicator.
Token gaps: `on-warning` is missing from the appendix, and colours are not mapped into `--color-*` @theme utilities.
The '12px floor' is contradicted by its own 11/500 bottom-bar labels and 10px avatar initials. The 52/44/36 row model is heavier than operator's.

This removes the biggest migration item and the marketing re-set while keeping every other Switchboard token.

Add clarity's lint rule banning arbitrary values (`text-[9px]`, `bg-[#…]`, `rounded-[9px]`) and raw Tailwind palette classes in app code, plus a codemod from `.btn-*` and bespoke buttons to the one Button.

From voice: `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));` with a single theme mechanism (a pre-hydration script sets `html.dark` from System/Light/Dark). Stop duplicating token blocks under a prefers-color-scheme media query (fixes DESIGN-SYSTEM-11/F-VIS-021).

From clarity: build the Readiness path as one component with page, popover, inline and horizontal variants. Use it to render Switchboard's 'Finish setup (2 of 4)', the pre-flight card rows (flow and version, number, calling hours, DND, recently called, cost vs wallet), the Publish sheet's validation checklist and the call-state stepper. From voice: the blocking-notice rule. An amber inline `role=status` notice appears only on pages whose primary task is blocked (Cockpit, Leads call actions, Publish), and never as a global bar. It complements the status line's ambient role.
From voice (later phase, data permitting): the mini conversation line in the Call reports detail scrubber, but only where per-turn start and end times exist. Hide it otherwise, and never fake it.
must_fix: Separate keyboard focus from selection everywhere, because all three directions conflate them. Focus is a 2px `outline` in --focus with a 2px offset. Selection is accent-soft fill plus a 1px accent border (or an inset bar on rows). On flow nodes, when a node is both focused and selected it shows both treatments. Never use the same outline for both.

Add `@media (forced-colors: active)` rules; none of the three specimens has any. Draw focus rings with `outline` (not box-shadow), and give ports, selected nodes, tags, the live dot, the status line and dashed fallback edges system-colour fallbacks (Highlight, CanvasText, ButtonBorder) so Windows High Contrast users keep state.

Fix font resolution before anything else: next/font variables go on `<html>` (F-VIS-008/DESIGN-SYSTEM-07). Budget fonts at 3 families at most, variable where available, with subset axes (no full wdth 75-125 ranges). Load Devanagari only via unicode-range, preload only the regular UI sans, and use `display: swap` with size-adjusted fallback metrics to avoid layout shift.

Put an automated contrast test in CI for every foreground/background token pair in both themes, plus visual-regression snapshots of both themes (DESIGN-SYSTEM-09). Known traps to lock out: text-3 on surface-3 (voice 4.45, clarity 4.49), solid warning as a standalone indicator (2.19 on white), and dark accent-hover with a white label (4.72, which is too close to the limit).

Make the 12px floor real and write down the exceptions. Allow at most caps-11/600 for table headers and canvas phase labels. Bottom-bar labels, keycaps, avatar initials and step markers go to 12px, and canvas text is counter-scaled to at least 12px on screen at every zoom (F-FLOW-008; clarity lacks this).

Keep live regions quiet. Exclude the status line's call timer, wallet decrement and cost-so-far from aria-live. Announce only state changes (Live, Ended, Low balance, Couldn't save), debounced, and only final transcript turns, throttled to one every 2 s or slower. Use a proper region label rather than overloading `contentinfo` with dynamic content.

Set a chrome budget at 1366x768 and 1280x720. Header, tabs, toolbar, table header, pager and status line together must still show at least 10 Leads rows in Standard density. At 720px height or less, collapse the status line into the header chip.

Treat touch as its own input on the canvas. On `pointer: coarse` at 1024px or wider (tablets in landscape), give ports and handles 44px hit areas or route connecting through the Outline and Go-to selects. The 24px hit areas are desktop-only.

Sequence the backend before the truthful UI: draft and published revisions, If-Match/409, server-side validation (422), server pagination (F-QA-005) and leg de-duplication (F-QA-006). Until they ship, the interim UI must not show 'Draft' or 'Saved' states it cannot guarantee (F-FLOW-001, F-QA-002).

Drive the rail tooltip, mobile tab label, H1, `<title>` and ⌘K from one nav config (DESIGN-SYSTEM-19). Keep renames minimal (Cockpit, Meetings) with permanent redirects. Keep an old-token alias layer (`--saffron` → `--accent` and so on) for one release, then delete it along with the 36 keyframes and the glass, grid and noise tokens.

Protect state colours for colour-vision deficiency. The accent must never read as 'live' or 'success'. Every state keeps a dot or icon plus a word, and if a teal or peacock accent is ever chosen instead of Neel, test the accent against success green under deuteranopia simulation (luminance ratio is only 1.15 in clarity).

Per-flow layout orientation. Offer left-to-right as the default for new flows and a one-click 'Re-layout as draft' for the 16 existing top-down flows. Never re-layout a live flow silently or on open, and never persist theme or viewport-driven changes to the flow (DESIGN-SYSTEM-08: a theme toggle currently fires PUT /api/flows).
